title: larkspur-manufacturing-post-optimize-savings-playbook
content:
Executive summary:
This is a customer-specific before/after analysis for Larkspur Manufacturing (mid-market, supply-chain assistant product). The workbook we ran through Redwood Optimize recommendations shows an expected 58–68% reduction in monthly inference cost depending on rollout aggressiveness, with minimal user-facing latency regressions (p50 increase <= 15ms) and no detected quality regressions on the core prompt set (n=120 gold prompts). This doc captures assumptions, the baseline, recommended change set, expected $$ impacts, a short rollout plan, and open questions.

High-level baseline (observed over last 30 days):
- Monthly active users (MAU): 12,400 (product analytics)
- Avg realtime request rate: 18 req/s (peak 50 req/s for 30m window)
- Monthly tokens generated: ~1.9B output tokens (plus ~0.5B input tokens) -> 2.4B total tokens
- Embedding calls (batch): 420k per month (512-dim)
- Model mix (30-day):
  * rw-13B-dense (safety/summary): 42% of tokens
  * rw-7B-balanced (dialogue & assistant): 38%
  * rw-30B-high-fidelity (few-shot planning, heavy prompts): 20%
- Baseline infra & pricing: hosted per-token rates modeled on current Redwood pricing grid; baseline monthly inference spend = $142,300 (tokens + embeddings + small overhead for network & storage). Latency p50 across endpoints: 170ms; p95: 420ms.

Key pain points uncovered in baseline profiling:
- Small subset of long-sequence planning prompts (8% of requests) disproportionately drive rw-30B usage and KV-cache churn (long prefix lengths).
- Embedding pipeline is single-threaded and sends many small batches late in the window (suboptimal batching yields +28% embedding cost).
- No prefix caching for repeated boilerplate in order-confirmation flows (5–7% of requests could have used prefix cache).

Redwood Optimize recommendations applied (summarized):
1) Model re-routing by policy: route low-criticality, high-volume requests (e.g., status checks, small formatting prompts) to rw-7B-quant (4-bit) model variant.
2) Quantization & kernel profile: switch rw-13B workloads to rw-13B-q4f16 for high-throughput endpoints where we observed no quality delta in evals.
3) Prefix/KV caching: enable request-level prefix caching for the order-confirmation and billing templates; TTL 24h, cache hit target 40% first week.
4) Embedding batching: enable batcher with target batch size 256 and max wait 25ms; move to async background pipeline for bulk embedding requests (nightly jobs where possible).
5) Dynamic reserved capacity: reserve a modest Dedicated slot during predictable peak windows (5–8pm local) and autoscale for other times with cheaper preemptible pools.
6) Canary and regression evals: run narrow eval set (n=120) and human spot-checking for first 2k responses post-change.

Estimated impact (after rollout, conservative vs aggressive):
- Conservative rollout (gradual, limited to non-critical routes + caching):
  * Token cost reduction: 38%
  * Embedding cost reduction: 22% (due to batching improvements)
  * Net monthly spend: $92,700 (~35% savings vs baseline)
- Aggressive rollout (wider model quantization + larger cache targets + reserved capacity optimization):
  * Token cost reduction: 62%
  * Embedding: 40%
  * Net monthly spend: $48,900 (~65.6% savings)

Detailed before/after snapshot (monthly):
- Baseline token spend: $120,100; embedding: $18,200; other infra: $4,000 -> total $142,300
- Post-optimize (conservative): token: $74,500; embedding: $14,200; infra: $4,000 -> $92,700
- Post-optimize (aggressive): token: $39,100; embedding: $10,300; infra: $4,000 -> $53,400 (note: we budgeted $4k for storage/network; final invoice may vary)

Quality and latency tradeoffs observed in sandbox tests (subset results):
- rw-13B-dense -> rw-13B-q4f16: ROUGE/L equivalent within 1.2 points on summaries; human A/B judge preferred dense in 12% of cases (mostly subtle factual phrasing).
- rw-30B-heavy planning -> route partial contexts to rw-13B-q4 with fallback to rw-30B for >75% confidence mismatch: reduced average latency for planning endpoints from 680ms -> 420ms at p50; p95 remained higher for the forced fallbacks.
- rw-7B -> rw-7B-quant: negligible quality delta for single-turn user queries; CPU/GPU throughput increased ~1.6x in our bench.

Sensitivity analysis (simplified):
- If embedding batch sizes remain small (avg batch size 64 instead of 256) -> embedding savings drop from 40% to ~12% and overall savings fall by ~8–10 percentage points.
- If cache hit rate <20% in week 1 -> savings cut by ~5–7k/month.
- If peak traffic grows 40% (seasonal event) and reserved capacity not increased -> p95 latency penalties and more fallbacks, increasing token spend by ~18%.

Implementation plan (rough, 6–8 weeks):
- Week 0: stakeholder sync + acceptance criteria (product + CS + infra) (owner: Priya)
- Week 1: enable rw-7B-quant test route for non-critical endpoints; deploy embedding batcher config to staging (owner: Jon)
- Week 2: enable prefix cache for templates in staging; run full regression evals and human spot checks (owner: Marta)
- Week 3: canary to 10% traffic; monitor quality metrics & latency (owner: Ravi)
- Week 4: expand to 50% with automatic fallback rules; confirm economics in Billing sandbox (owner: Priya)
- Week 5: full rollout with monitoring alerts & SLOs; handoff to ops and customer success for regular check-ins (owner: Jon & Marta)
- Instrumentation tasks: add prompt-level tagging, token-level cost attribution and per-route dashboard (linked artifact: JIRA-7892).

Open questions and risks (notes to self):
- User acceptance: product wants a 0% visible UX regressions SLA for summaries; how conservative must we be with quantization for those endpoints? (Action: prioritize human evals for summaries set)
- Billing model edge case: if customer moves to Dedicated mid-rollout, commit pricing changes may alter ROI math; need finance sign-off.
- Legal/compliance: cached user content in prefix cache might contain PII for 0.6% of requests — must confirm TTL & redaction policy with security.

Quick wins (<=2 weeks):
- Turn on embedding batcher with target size 256 for all bulk ingestion jobs (expected immediate ~20% embedding reduction).
- Enable prefix cache only for templates and stable text flows (quick config, low quality risk).
- Add basic cost attribution tags in request path to split by feature (saves manual reconciliation time).

Metrics to monitor post-rollout (minimum):
- Token spend by route (daily)
- Embedding cost per 100k calls (daily)
- Cache hit rate by template (hourly)
- Eval quality delta (weekly human spot checks + automated metrics)
- Latency p50/p95 per route (hourly)
- Rollback triggers: >2% drop in automated quality metric OR >20% increase in p95 latency for 3 consecutive hours

Appendix A — test eval brief (short):
- N=120 gold prompts created by product + CS; split across summaries (40), planning (30), confirmations (20), embeddings (30).
- A/B blind human judging for 200 samples across rolled changes.
- Evaluation metrics: correctness (binary), readability (1–5), hallucination flag (binary).

Appendix B — quick cost calc (worked example):
- baseline token unit price assumed: $0.000050 per token (weighted by model tiers) -> 2.4B tokens => $120k approx
- rw-13B-q4f16 expected unit price: 0.6x baseline per-token for that class due to quantization + kernel speedups

To do (immediate):
- [ ] Share this playbook with product + CS for sign-off (Priya)
- [ ] Open JIRA for embedding batcher infra changes and link to billing sandbox (Jon)
- [ ] Security review for cache redaction and TTL (Marta)
- [ ] Prepare communication plan for customers in case of visible regressions (Ravi)

Notes / rough thoughts: this doc is intended as a pragmatic, customer-specific playbook that product & SEs can use to justify a Redwood Optimize pilot. Keep an eye on embedding batch latency — if that creeps up, revert to async-only ingestion for heavy night jobs.

End of playbook.

(Internal draft — contains rough numbers; finalize spreadsheet and sensitivity runs in linked Confluence before presenting to customer.)
